_doc: Non-crypto fixtures the in-process differential oracle cannot execute for a STRUCTURAL reason (not a missing crypto witness). Post-mortem remediation #1 added a real deploy->call->Spend path (conformance/witnesses/real-crypto/ via runar-testing runStatefulSpend) and MOVED every stateful fixture whose continuation could be driven and re-validated on @bsv/sdk Spend with a real checkPreimage binding out of this list. The free-text `reason` is for humans; the machine-checked truth of each entry's claim lives in its `coveredBy` field (see coverage-claims.test.ts) — membership in this list is NOT itself treated as coverage. See conformance/witnesses/README.md.

inapplicable.reason: UnsafeSmartContract asm({body:'51'}) raw-script intrinsic is not implemented by the ANF interpreter (source-semantics engine reports 'Unknown function: asm'), so the differential / real-crypto oracles cannot execute it. Instead the compiled OP_1 is executed directly on the go-sdk Bitcoin Script engine (anyone-can-spend, empty unlocking → clean TRUE); deliberately no reject case, since universal acceptance is the contract's semantics.
BabyBear field proof-system primitive is Go-only (compilers:[go]); no TypeScript Stack-IR codegen, compile() cannot emit deployed bytes
BabyBear quartic-extension proof-system primitive is Go-only (compilers:[go]); no TypeScript codegen

sendToScript(): a TWO-output method — addRawOutput(1000, scriptBytes) plus the addOutput(0, count) state continuation. The SDK deploy->call->Spend path (real-crypto/ style) funds a single continuation output; it does not fund/emit the separate 1000-sat raw output, so a real Spend rejects (checkPreimage output binding fails). RESOLVED (audit P0 follow-up): the SDK deploy->call path still can't compose this, but conformance/script_execution_test.go now hand-builds the exact 3-output tx (raw output, state continuation, change) via executeScriptWithTx and gets a genuine tx-context accept/reject differential against the compiled Bitcoin Script bytes — TestRawOutput_ScriptExecution_Accept (raw output present) and TestRawOutput_ScriptExecution_Reject_RawOutputAbsent (raw output omitted from the real tx while the unlocking script still claims it) — superseding the ANF-interpreter-only anf-cross-tier-parity coverage below as the primary claim.

spend(): branched mutation of count + a fixed-width ByteString state field re-encodes state via OP_NUM2BIN. Driven through the SDK call() path the recomputed continuation width does not match (OP_NUM2BIN 'size not large enough') — the harness cannot reconstruct the exact branched serialisation. FOLLOW-UP: port the Go witness construction.

coveredBy.note: both branches (then/else of the len(scratch)-driven conditional) executed via the ANF interpreter with realistic args; TS tier only, not a full Bitcoin Script byte execution, and this particular fixture's spec is accept-only by design (both arms succeed — the branching logic itself is what's under test, not a checkSig/checkPreimage guard).

inapplicable.reason: payBond() is a TERMINAL StatefulSmartContract method that asserts output 0 is a bond P2PKH via requireOutputP2PKH(0, ...) with no state mutation, so there is no state continuation and output 0 is free. The SDK deploy->call->Spend path does not compose an external bond output, so there is no go-script-exec accept/reject differential; covered instead by the ANF interpreter (1 accept + 2 reject: correct witness, wrong PKH bytes, wrong hashOutputs) across all 7 tiers. NOTE: the earlier variant that mixed requireOutputP2PKH(0) with a state mutation (the implicit single-output continuation ALSO claiming output 0, making it permanently unspendable) is now a COMPILE-TIME ERROR — see the guard in packages/runar-compiler/src/passes/03-typecheck.ts and TestIntentOutputP2PKH_GuardRejectsMutatingVariant in conformance/script_execution_test.go.

coveredBy.note: 1 accept + 2 reject (wrong PKH bytes, wrong hashOutputs) executed via the ANF interpreter with witness-injected serialised outputs (TestContract.setSerialisedOutputs / setMockPreimageBytes), mirrored per-tier in the runar-{go,rs,py,zig,rb,java} intent interpreter tests. Not a full Bitcoin Script byte execution.

inapplicable.reason: bind(): extractPrevOutputScript(0, expectedHash) asserts hash256(witness) === expectedHash, a constructor-baked readonly field — the witness-bridge pattern documented in docs/cross-covenant-pattern.md (it does NOT itself introspect input 0's real prevout script; only the current input's own BIP-143 preimage fields are available to Bitcoin Script). RESOLVED (audit P0 follow-up): the earlier 'circular' framing assumed input 0 must be the contract's own (self-referential, hence impossible) UTXO; conformance/script_execution_test.go instead builds a real TWO-input transaction where input 0 carries an independent companion prevout (whose real locking script is the witness) and input 1 carries the contract's own UTXO being spent — TestIntentPrevOutputScript_ScriptExecution_Accept (witness bytes hash to expectedHash, genuinely equal to input 0's real prevout script) and TestIntentPrevOutputScript_ScriptExecution_Reject_WrongWitness (tampered witness bytes) — a real tx-context accept/reject differential against the compiled Bitcoin Script bytes.
